sections.h2: What sets a Cherry Hill home sale apart from a typical New Jersey closing?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill sellers face two separate township inspections before closing, one covering the property's exterior and one covering smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and each is booked through a different office. Booking both early keeps the closing date from slipping.

The township is large, mostly owner-occupied and built largely in the decades after World War II, so the typical seller owns a single-family house on a suburban lot with trees, fences, driveways and sidewalks that the township cares about. This page walks through the inspections, the tax calendar, the county recording charges and a worked transfer-fee example so you can set a realistic closing date.

sections.h2: How big is Cherry Hill and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill covers about 24 square miles of Camden County, which makes it the county's most populous municipality. It began as Delaware Township in 1844, and in 1961 took the Cherry Hill name from a local farm. Quaker settlers arrived in the late 1600s, the first small cluster was Colestown, and 19th-century farms supplied produce to the Campbell's soup plant across the river in Camden. Growth then jumped after World War II, from about 10,400 residents in 1950 to 31,500 in 1960 and 64,400 in 1970.

Its neighborhoods include Ashland, Barclay, Erlton, Greentree, Kingston Estates, Springdale, Woodcrest and the area around Cherry Hill Mall. Pennsauken Creek marks the eastern line with Burlington County, the Cooper River runs along the southern border beside Route 70, and Haddonfield, Collingswood and Voorhees sit across those lines.

sections.h2: Which roads, transit lines and schools matter to Cherry Hill buyers?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill is built around highway access to Philadelphia. Interstate 295 has three exits in the township, including exit 31, which leads directly to the Woodcrest PATCO station, and Routes 38, 41, 70 and 154 cross it. Township roads total about 309 miles, of which the township itself maintains roughly 247. NJ Transit buses reach Philadelphia on the 317, 404 and 406 routes, and the Atlantic City Line stops at the Cherry Hill station.

Schools are the other big talking point. Cherry Hill Public Schools operates 19 schools with about 10,800 students in the 2023 to 2024 school year, including two traditional high schools, Cherry Hill High School East and Cherry Hill High School West, three middle schools and 12 elementary schools. Private options include Camden Catholic High School and the King's Christian School.

  • Mention the PATCO station and I-295 exits in your listing if you are close to them.
  • Name the elementary school zone, since buyers search by it.
  • Note any Cooper River or creek frontage and have the drainage history ready.

sections.h2: What are the two Cherry Hill inspections before closing?
sections.html:
A seller here needs a Certificate of Continued Occupancy from the township and a smoke alarm and carbon monoxide compliance certificate from the fire department. A single-family sale cannot reach closing without them, and they are separate appointments with separate costs.

The occupancy certificate comes from Community Development, which handles property maintenance, at 820 Mercer Street, Room 202. The property maintenance officer looks at exterior areas only. The township lists these items:

  • Sidewalks, driveways and fences.
  • Trees and natural growth.
  • Sanitation and exhaust vents.
  • Grading and drainage, including where sump pumps discharge.
  • Accessory structures and ground surface hazards.

The inspection costs $100, payable ahead of the visit, and you can apply online, in person or by mail. Online applications need office approval before a payment request is emailed, cancellations after payment are not refunded, and the property maintenance line is 856-834-3364. Some condominiums and townhomes are excluded, and the township posts a list of properties that skip the inspection.

The fire department certificate is a different step. It is required for one- and two-family homes before settlement, and sellers are asked to request the appointment three to four weeks early. If the home passes and payment is made, the certificate is handed over at the visit; temporary certificates are not issued, and fire extinguishers are no longer required. The fire department's inspection line is (856) 429-7441. Because the two appointments run on separate calendars, book both the week the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Does the township help with move-out trash after a Cherry Hill sale?
sections.html:
Yes, Cherry Hill offers a one-time courtesy collection for house clean-outs after a sale, covering furniture, carpets, bedding and similar household items. Proof that you applied for a Continued Certificate of Occupancy is required before Public Works will schedule it, pickups happen on Fridays, and the number to call is 856-424-4422.

The same guidelines say no trash or recycling service goes to dwellings under construction, vacant lots or properties lacking a valid certificate of occupancy, so a vacant house waiting on its paperwork may go without pickup. Plan the clean-out around the certificate date, and keep contractor debris out of the cart, because construction waste generated by a contractor has to be hauled away by that contractor.

sections.h2: When are Cherry Hill property taxes due and who collects them?
sections.html:
The four installments land on the first of August, November, February and May, and a ten-day grace period rolls forward to the next business day if it ends on a weekend or holiday. The township mails two bills a year: July covers the third and fourth installments, and January covers the first and second. Money has to be in the tax office by the last grace day, because postmarks do not count.

Late payments accrue 8 percent a year up to $1,500 of arrears and 18 percent on any amount beyond that, running from the original due date. The tax collector also bills sewer rent: residential sewer is a flat annual fee due April 1, with a 10 percent discount for owners 60 or older who live in the property. Ask the tax office at 856-488-7880 for a closing figure that includes any sewer balance. The office gathers money for the school district, the fire district and Camden County along with the township, so the bill you pay includes those shares.

Appeals follow state deadlines, April 1 or May 1 after a revaluation, and go to the Camden County Board of Taxation.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer fee and where does the deed get filed?
sections.html:
The Camden County Clerk files the deed, and the seller owes the state realty transfer fee when it is filed. Above $350,000 the state schedule runs $2.90 per $500 for the first $150,000, $4.25 per $500 for the slice from $150,000 to $200,000 and $4.80 per $500 for the slice from $200,000 to $550,000. On a $400,000 price, those slices add up to about $3,215: $870, then $425, then $1,920. Confirm the figure with your closing attorney, since senior, disabled and low-income rates run lower.

The county's recording schedule lists $30 for page one of a deed, $10 for every added page, a $10 abstracting fee and a $5 homeless trust fund charge, with a $55 floor. Camden County's online land records start in 1978, and the clerk's office answers at 856-225-5300. A New Jersey resident signs a residency certification at closing, while a seller who is leaving the state prepays estimated income tax, so tell your attorney early if you are relocating.

faqs.q: Are inspections required to sell in Cherry Hill?
faqs.a: Yes, two of them. The township requires a Certificate of Continued Occupancy for single-family resale, and the fire department requires a smoke alarm and carbon monoxide compliance certificate before settlement.

faqs.q: What does the Cherry Hill resale inspection cost?
faqs.a: The occupancy inspection is $100, paid before the inspector arrives. The fire department sets its own charges, which are posted on its checklist.

faqs.q: How early should the Cherry Hill fire inspection be scheduled?
faqs.a: Three to four weeks before settlement. The certificate is given at the appointment if the home complies and payment is made, and temporary certificates are not available.

faqs.q: What are the Cherry Hill tax installment dates?
faqs.a: August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A ten-day grace period applies, and the money must reach the tax office by then because postmarks do not count.

faqs.q: Who files a Cherry Hill deed?
faqs.a: The Camden County Clerk. The posted schedule lists $30 for page one of a deed, $10 for each added page, a $10 abstracting fee and a $5 homeless trust fund charge.
